added: #Look for a space to store the tub’s pump and wiring. Whirlpool tubs require extensive electrical wiring and a pump, which need to be within a few feet of the tub. If you have a closet or cabinet adjacent to the tub, it can be stored there. If not, you’ll need to get an alcove tub with an apron or a drop-in tub that’s built into a deck. These styles will hide the electrical equipment.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Choose between water jets or air jets. Water-jet whirlpool tubs force water through jets, giving more pressure and a forceful massage. In air-jet whirlpool tubs, air is forced through tiny holes for a lighter massage. A combination whirlpool tub uses both, but will be more expensive and may use more energy.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]

These styles will hide the electrical equipment.<ref>http://www.consumersearch.com/bathtubs/whirlpool-bathtubs</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Choose between water jets or air jets. Water-jet whirlpool tubs force water through jets, giving more pressure and a forceful massage. In air-jet whirlpool tubs, air is forced through tiny holes for a lighter massage. A combination whirlpool tub uses both, but will be more expensive and may use more energy.<ref>http://www.consumersearch.com/bathtubs/whirlpool-bathtubs</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]

added: #Look for a space to store the tub’s pump and wiring. Whirlpool tubs require extensive electrical wiring and a pump, which need to be within a few feet of the tub. If you have a closet or cabinet adjacent to the tub, it can be stored there. If not, you’ll need to get an alcove tub with an apron or a drop-in tub that’s built into a deck. These styles will hide the electrical equipment.<ref>http://www.consumersearch.com/bathtubs/whirlpool-bathtubs</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Measure the space where the tub will go. Figure out the length, width, and depth of the space you’d like the tub to fill. And unless you’re building a brand new bathroom, get the measurements of the bathroom doorway to be sure your new tub will fit through it.<ref>http://www.bhg.com/bathroom/shower-bath/buying-a-tub/</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 2 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Note where the current tub’s drain is. Unless you’re doing extensive renovations, your new tub’s drain will need to be in the same location as the old one. Note whether the drain is oriented left, right, or center, and look for a new tub that will match it.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 3 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Determine your water heater’s capacity. This is usually printed somewhere on the side of your water heater. Whirlpool tubs require a lot of hot water, so if you have a particularly small unit, you may need to upgrade to a larger one. Aim for your water heater to have at least ⅔ the capacity of any tub you buy.<ref>http://www.bhg.com/bathroom/shower-bath/buying-a-tub/</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 4 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Choose between water jets or air jets. Water-jet whirlpool tubs force water through jets, giving more pressure and a forceful massage. In air-jet whirlpool tubs, air is forced through tiny holes for a lighter massage. A combination whirlpool tub uses both, but will be more expensive and may use more energy.<ref>http://www.consumersearch.com/bathtubs/whirlpool-bathtubs</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 5 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Decide which material suits your needs. Acrylic tubs are the most popular, but fiberglass is the lightest and cheapest material. Cast iron is durable and retains heat well, but it’s incredibly heavy. You’ll need to install additional floor support if you opt for cast iron.<ref>http://www.bhg.com/bathroom/shower-bath/buying-a-tub/</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Look for special features like chromotherapy. Some whirlpool tubs have colored lights built into the sides that offer light therapy to help balance your energy while you bathe. Others have self-cleaning jets that blow air out after every use to dry the lines and prevent mold.<ref>https://www.houzz.com/ideabooks/12590746/list/dreaming-of-a-spa-tub-at-home-read-this-pro-advice-first</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Choose a design that meets your family’s needs. If you have elderly family members or anyone with mobility issues in your house, get a walk-in tub. There are tubs with doors and grab bars to make getting in and out easier. If you have small children, think about getting a shallower tub with sides that are easier to climb over.<ref>https://www.bobvila.com/articles/how-to-choose-a-bathtub/#.WWWXIDPMySM</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 8 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Create a budget. Make a budget that outlines how much you can spend on the tub, the fixtures, and the installation. Compare costs of tubs with and without special features. For example, a white tub offered at $1450 could increase to $1500 if you want it in beige. Decide how important each feature is to you so you can prioritize.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Visit a showroom. Whether you want to buy from a small, local dealer or a large home supply store, you need to be able to examine a variety of tubs before buying one. Something may look good online, but it could be uncomfortable once you climb inside.<ref>http://www.bhg.com/bathroom/shower-bath/buying-a-tub/</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Sit in several tubs. Make sure the size and shape of the tub and the placement of controls, armrests, and jets are comfortable. If you and your significant other plan to both use the tub at the same time, you should both climb inside to make sure it’s roomy enough.<ref>https://www.houzz.com/ideabooks/12590746/list/dreaming-of-a-spa-tub-at-home-read-this-pro-advice-first</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Check reviews online. Check out Consumer Reports and other rating sites to be sure there aren’t any common complaints about the tub you like. Also check for complaints against the manufacturer and dealer, especially if they are new or unfamiliar to you.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 12 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Consult contractors. There’s a lot that goes into installing a whirlpool tub, including complex electrical work. You may need to have an additional fuse installed or make plumbing modifications. Call an electrician or a general contractor and give them the specifications for the tub that interests you. They’ll let you know if any work needs to be done before installation.<ref>https://www.houzz.com/ideabooks/12590746/list/dreaming-of-a-spa-tub-at-home-read-this-pro-advice-first</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 13 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Purchase a faucet and other hardware. Once you've selected your tub, then you can purchase a faucet and accessories like a handheld sprayer. Different types of tubs require different types of hardware, so be sure that you purchase a free-standing tub filler if you've chosen a free-standing tub.<ref>https://www.houzz.com/ideabooks/12590746/list/dreaming-of-a-spa-tub-at-home-read-this-pro-advice-first</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 14 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Schedule installation services. Typically, the business you buy the tub from will offer installation services for an additional fee. Schedule this at the time of purchase, or just wait and hire your own plumber or general contractor to do the job.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 15 Version 2.jpg|center]]

These styles will hide the electrical equipment.<ref>http://www.consumersearch.com/bathtubs/whirlpool-bathtubs</ref>
#*Pump size will depend upon how many jets your tub has, but you may need up to 2 square feet (.6 square meters) of storage space for the pump.
#*A standard tub is about 30 to 32 inches (76 to 81 cm) wide, 60 inches (152 cm) long, and 14 to 20 inches (35 to 50 cm) deep.

#*Most tubs should fit through a standard 32-inch (81-cm) bathroom door. But some older homes have narrower doors, so measure to be sure.<ref>https://www.houzz.com/ideabooks/26567086/list/key-measurements-to-make-the-most-of-your-bathroom</ref>
#*For example, a 75-gallon (284-liter) tub should have a 50-gallon (189-liter) water heater.
#*The smallest water heater you should have is between 30 and 40 gallons (113 and 151 liters). If budget's not an issue and you have a large family, you can get a 100-gallon (378-liter) water heater.
#*One drawback of water-jet and combination tubs is that you can’t use bath salts or oils, as these will damage the pumping mechanism.
#*Another water-jet and combination tub drawback is that some water stays in the jets, and mold can develop if they’re not regularly cleaned out.
#*A cast-iron tub can cost well over $1500, but an acrylic tub will typically be less than $1000.

#Create a budget. Make a budget that outlines how much you can spend on the tub, the fixtures, and the installation. Compare costs of tubs with and without special features. For example, a white tub offered at $1450 could increase to $1500 if you want it in beige. Decide how important each feature is to you so you can prioritize.
#*Do some research to see if a tub is offered at a better price from a different seller. Just be aware that a lower price might mean less customer service.

added: Whirlpool tubs can provide a relaxing, spa-like experience right at home. Many homeowners are upgrading to these jetted tubs as they embark on bathroom renovations. But if you're thinking of buying one, you have many factors to consider, such as space requirements, design options, and the complex installation process.

#Measure the space where the tub will go. Figure out the length, width, and depth of the space you’d like the tub to fill. And unless you’re building a brand new bathroom, get the measurements of the bathroom doorway to be sure your new tub will fit through it.<ref>http://www.bhg.com/bathroom/shower-bath/buying-a-tub/</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 1.jpg|center]]

#Note where the current tub’s drain is. Unless you’re doing extensive renovations, your new tub’s drain will need to be in the same location as the old one. Note whether the drain is oriented left, right, or center, and look for a new tub that will match it.

#Determine your water heater’s capacity. This is usually printed somewhere on the side of your water heater. Whirlpool tubs require a lot of hot water, so if you have a particularly small unit, you may need to upgrade to a larger one. Aim for your water heater to have at least ⅔ the capacity of any tub you buy.<ref>http://www.bhg.com/bathroom/shower-bath/buying-a-tub/</ref>

#Choose between water jets or air jets. Water-jet whirlpool tubs force water through jets, giving more pressure and a forceful massage. In air-jet whirlpool tubs, air is forced through tiny holes for a lighter massage. A combination whirlpool tub uses both, but will be more expensive and may use more energy.<ref>http://www.consumersearch.com/bathtubs/whirlpool-bathtubs</ref>
#*Another water-jet drawback is that some water stays in the jets, and mold can develop if they’re not regularly cleaned out.

#Decide which material suits your needs. Acrylic tubs are the most popular, but fiberglass is the lightest and cheapest material. Cast iron is durable and retains heat well, but it’s incredibly heavy. You’ll need to install additional floor support if you opt for cast iron.<ref>http://www.bhg.com/bathroom/shower-bath/buying-a-tub/</ref>

#Choose a design that meets your family’s needs. If you have elderly family members or anyone with mobility issues in your house, get a walk-in tub. There are tubs with doors and grab bars to make getting in and out easier. If you have small children, think about getting a shallower tub with sides that are easier to climb over.<ref>https://www.bobvila.com/articles/how-to-choose-a-bathtub/#.WWWXIDPMySM</ref>

#Visit a showroom. Whether you want to buy from a small, local dealer or a large home supply store, you need to be able to examine a variety of tubs before buying one. Something may look good online, but it could be uncomfortable once you climb inside.<ref>http://www.bhg.com/bathroom/shower-bath/buying-a-tub/</ref>

#Consult contractors. There’s a lot that goes into installing a whirlpool tub, including complex electrical work. You may need to have an additional fuse installed or make plumbing modifications. Call an electrician or a general contractor and give them the specifications for the tub that interests you. They’ll let you know if any work needs to be done before installation.<ref>https://www.houzz.com/ideabooks/12590746/list/dreaming-of-a-spa-tub-at-home-read-this-pro-advice-first</ref>
#*Also ask your contractor to build a deck if you'll be purchasing a drop-in tub.

added: Whirlpool tubs can provide a relaxing, spa-like experience right at home. Many homeowners are upgrading to these jetted tubs as they embark on bathroom renovations. But there are many factors to consider when buying one, such as space requirements, design options, and the complex installation process.
[[Category:Swimming Pools Spas and Hot Tubs]]
== Steps ==
===Assessing Your Space===

#Look for a space to store the tub’s pump and wiring. Whirlpool tubs require extensive electrical wiring and a pump, which needs to be within a few feet of the tub. If you have a closet or cabinet adjacent to the tub, it can be stored there. If not, you’ll need to get an alcove tub with an apron or a drop-in tub that’s built into a deck. These styles will hide the electrical equipment.<ref>http://www.consumersearch.com/bathtubs/whirlpool-bathtubs</ref>
#*If you have an adjacent space to store the pump, you can opt for a freestanding tub like a claw-foot tub.

#Measure the space where the tub will go. Figure out the length, width, and depth of the space you’d like the tub to fill. And unless you’re building a brand new bathroom, get the measurements of the bathroom doorway to be sure your new tub will fit through it.<ref>https://www.plumbingsupply.com/ed-tub.html</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 1.jpg|center]]
#*If you’re interested in a drop-in tub, keep in mind that the deck it drops into will take up a few extra inches of bathroom space all the way around the tub.

#Note where the current tub’s drain is. Unless you’re doing extensive renovations, your new tub’s drain will need to be in the same location as the old one. Note whether the drain is oriented left, right, or center, and look for a new tub that will match it.<ref>https://www.lowes.com/projects/bed-and-bath/tubs-whirlpools-buying-guide/project</ref>

#Determine your water heater’s capacity. This is usually printed somewhere on the side of your water heater. Whirlpool tubs require a lot of hot water, so if you have a particularly small unit, you may need to upgrade to a larger one. Aim for your water heater to have at least ⅔ the capacity of any tub you buy.<ref>https://www.overstock.com/guides/whirlpool-bathtub-fact-sheet</ref>
===Choosing Tub Features===

#Choose between water jets or air jets. Water-jet whirlpool tubs force water through jets, giving more pressure and a forceful massage. In air-jet whirlpool tubs, air is forced through tiny holes for a lighter massage. A combination whirlpool tub uses both, but will be more expensive and may use more energy.<ref>https://www.overstock.com/guides/whirlpool-bathtub-fact-sheet</ref>
#*One drawback of a water-jet tub is that you can’t use bath salts or oils, as these will damage the pumping mechanism.
#*Another water-jet drawback is that some water stays in the jets, and mold can develop if they’re not regularly cleaned out.<ref>http://www.consumersearch.com/bathtubs/whirlpool-bathtubs</ref>

#Decide which material suits your needs. Acrylic tubs are the most popular, but fiberglass is the lightest and cheapest material. Cast iron is durable and retains heat well, but it’s incredibly heavy. You’ll need to install additional floor support if you opt for cast iron.<ref>https://www.lowes.com/projects/bed-and-bath/tubs-whirlpools-buying-guide/project</ref>

#Look for special features like chromotherapy. Some whirlpool tubs have colored lights built into the sides that offer light therapy to help balance your energy while you bathe. Others have self-cleaning jets that blow air out after every use to dry the lines and prevent mold.<ref>https://www.houzz.com/ideabooks/12590746/list/dreaming-of-a-spa-tub-at-home-read-this-pro-advice-first</ref>[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 7.jpg|center]]

#Choose a design that meets your family’s needs. If you have elderly family members or anyone with mobility issues in your house, get a walk-in tub. There are tubs with doors and grab bars to make getting in and out easier. If you have small children, think about getting a shallower tub with sides that are easier to climb over.<ref>https://www.lowes.com/projects/bed-and-bath/tubs-whirlpools-buying-guide/project</ref>
===Purchasing Your Tub===

#Visit a showroom. Whether you want to buy from a small, local dealer or a large home supply store, you need to be able to examine a variety of tubs before buying one. Something may look good online, but it could uncomfortable once you climb inside.<ref>https://www.houzz.com/ideabooks/12590746/list/dreaming-of-a-spa-tub-at-home-read-this-pro-advice-first</ref>

#Sit in several tubs. Make sure the size and shape of the tub and the placement of controls, armrests, and jets are comfortable. If you and your significant other plan to both use the tub at the same time, you should both climb inside to make sure it’s roomy enough.<ref>https://www.houzz.com/ideabooks/12590746/list/dreaming-of-a-spa-tub-at-home-read-this-pro-advice-first</ref>

#Check reviews online. Check out Consumer Reports and other rating sites to be sure there aren’t any common complaints about the tub you like. Also check for complaints against the manufacturer and dealer, especially if they are new or unfamiliar to you.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 9.jpg|center]]

#Consult contractors. There’s a lot that goes into installing a whirlpool tub, including complex electrical work. You may need to have an additional fuse installed or make plumbing modifications. Call an electrician or a general contractor and give them the specifications for the tub that interests you. They’ll let you know if any work needs to be done before installation.<ref>https://www.plumbingsupply.com/ed-tub.html</ref>
#*This is also a good time to ask a contractor to build a deck if you'll be purchasing a drop-in tub.

#Purchase a faucet and other hardware. Once you've selected your tub, then you can purchase a faucet and accessories like a handheld sprayer. Different types of tubs require different types of hardware, so be sure that you purchase a free-standing tub filler if you've chosen a free-standing tub.<ref>https://www.houzz.com/ideabooks/12590746/list/dreaming-of-a-spa-tub-at-home-read-this-pro-advice-first</ref>

#Schedule installation services. Typically the business you buy the tub from will offer installation services for an additional fee. Schedule this at the time of purchase, or just wait and hire your own plumber or general contractor to do the job.

While a whirlpool tub is in reach for many, the wide array of whirlpool tub design choices, as well various types of jet power and placement and other options can make figuring out how to buy a whirlpool tub feel like an overwhelming task. Make it easier by being familiar with the various types of whirlpool tubs and testing them out first-hand if possible.
[[Category:Swimming Pools Spas and Hot Tubs]]
== Steps ==
#Measure the space where the tub will be placed to determine what kind of whirlpool tub you should buy.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 1.jpg|center]]

#Determine whether you want a water-jet tub, air-jet tub, or a combination of the two. Water-jet whirlpool tubs force water through jets, giving more pressure and a forceful massage. In air-jet whirlpool tubs, air is forced through tiny holes for a lighter all-over massage. A combination whirlpool tub uses both, but may use more energy.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 2.jpg|center]]

#Find out how important bath salts and oils are to those who will be bathing in the tub. These cannot be used in a water-jet tub, since they can clog and damage the pump.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 3.jpg|center]]

#Figure out how the tub will be installed. Cast iron tubs may need added floor support, which will add to the cost of installation and make it more difficult to do yourself. Standard sizes fit into an existing tub space. Drop in units will require a custom surround to be built. Tubs with sides are the easiest to install, but are less flexible choices in the design of a bathroom.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 4.jpg|center]]
#Compare the size of the tub and your current hot water heater. Make sure the current tank holds enough hot water to fill the tub.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 5.jpg|center]]

#Test the unit in person if possible. Sit in the tub to make sure the size and shape of the tub and the placement of controls, armrests and jets are comfortable. The tub also should be easy to get in and out of. If possible, get a demonstration in a full, working tub.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 6.jpg|center]]

#Think about optional or unusual add-on options and designs. Some whirlpool tubs offer chromotherapy--colored lights--built into the tub at an additional cost. Clawfoot tubs offer a more vintage look with the modern twist of a whirlpool massage.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 7.jpg|center]]

#Decide what type of dealer you want to purchase from, and find out how to buy a whirlpool tub from the dealers in your area. Many tubs are available at large home supply stores or can be special ordered from them. Compare the cost and level of customer service and installation options to local dealers in your area.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 8.jpg|center]]

#Check reviews of the whirlpool tubs you are thinking about purchasing. Ask friends and family for recommendations and check out Consumer Reports and other rating sites. Check for complaints against the manufacturer and dealer, especially if they are new or unfamiliar ones.[[Image:Buy a Whirlpool Tub Step 9.jpg|center]]

Whirlpool tubs are becoming more of a standard in new homes and bathroom renovations, and lower prices make them very attainable. While a whirlpool tub is in reach for many, the wide array of whirlpool tub design choices, as well various types of jet power and placement and other options can make figuring out how to buy a whirlpool tub feel like an overwhelming task. Make it easier by being familiar with the various types of whirlpool tubs and testing them out first-hand if possible.
== Steps ==
# Measure the space where the tub will be placed to determine what kind of whirlpool tub you should buy.

# Determine whether you want a water-jet tub, air-jet tub, or a combination of the two. Water-jet whirlpool tubs force water through jets, giving more pressure and a forceful massage. In air-jet whirlpool tubs, air is forced through tiny holes for a lighter all-over massage. A combination whirlpool tub uses both, but may use more energy.
# Find out how important bath salts and oils are to those who will be bathing in the tub. These cannot be used in a water-jet tub, since they can clog and damage the pump.

# Figure out how the tub will be installed. Cast iron tubs may need added floor support, which will add to the cost of installation and make it more difficult to do yourself. Standard sizes fit into an existing tub space. Drop in units will require a custom surround to be built. Tubs with sides are the easiest to install, but are less flexible choices in the design of a bathroom.
# Compare the size of the tub and your current hot water heater. Make sure the current tank holds enough hot water to fill the tub.

# Test the unit in person if possible. Sit in the tub to make sure the size and shape of the tub and the placement of controls, armrests and jets are comfortable. The tub also should be easy to get in and out of. If possible, get a demonstration in a full, working tub.

# Think about optional or unusual add-on options and designs. Some whirlpool tubs offer chromotherapy--colored lights--built into the tub at an additional cost. Clawfoot tubs offer a more vintage look with the modern twist of a whirlpool massage.

# Decide what type of dealer you want to purchase from, and find out how to buy a whirlpool tub from the dealers in your area. Many tubs are available at large home supply stores or can be special ordered from them. Compare the cost and level of customer service and installation options to local dealers in your area.

# Check reviews of the whirlpool tubs you are thinking about purchasing. Ask friends and family for recommendations and check out Consumer Reports and other rating sites. Check for complaints against the manufacturer and dealer, especially if they are new or unfamiliar ones.
